author: reviewer
excerpt: Pick Which Days to Include: Control the accuracy of your report by choosing: All Days – Includes everything. Non-Empty Days – Excludes blank days. Complete Days – This shows only the days you've fully logged and marked as complete in your diary.
observation: Independent vendor source: the Cronometer blog post 'Get to Know Your Nutrition: A Look at Cronometer's Nutrition Report', published 22 March 2023 (it redirects to a URL with a trailing slash). It says the Nutrition Report shows average nutrient intake over a time frame, and the user can choose All Days, Non-Empty Days or Complete Days. It also suggests leaving out today if logging is unfinished, so averages stay accurate. Basic users can view up to one week before today; Gold users can set custom ranges.
limitations: Vendor blog, not a help-centre article, and not observed in the app. It covers the Nutrition Report rather than every Trends chart, and does not state the default option. I also tried the Cronometer help-centre article support.cronometer.com/hc/en-us/articles/360018569691, but it returned HTTP 403 (a bot check), so it is not recorded.
